note: Shared golden spec for callout recognition parity between the published renderer and line-based editor scanners. Byte-identical copies live in each consumer repo; bump `version` and update every copy together when semantics change. `published` and `editor` list the ordered callouts recognized in the input as {type, title} (empty = every blockquote stays a plain quote). `editorGate` marks cases the editor rejects via a non-scanner gate (e.g. code fences), so scanner-only harnesses skip the editor assertion.

cases.name: nested-inner-stays-plain
cases.note: v1 transforms top-level blockquotes only; the nested quote stays plain on both sides.

cases.name: code-fence-literal
cases.note: Inside a fence the line is code; the editor excludes it via the syntax tree, which pure scanners cannot see.

cases.name: header-on-second-line
cases.note: The marker only counts on the quote's first line.

cases.name: non-alpha-type
cases.note: Types are ASCII letters only; anything else stays a plain quote.

cases.name: markup-after-marker
cases.note: Recognition divergence (documented v1 limit): the published parser sees the first text node end at the marker, so `[!tip]**bold**` is a callout with a fallback title; the editor requires whitespace after the marker and keeps the quote plain.

cases.name: markup-mid-title
cases.note: Title divergence (documented v1 limit): published titles truncate at the first inline construct (the rest flows into the body); the editor titles the whole raw line.

cases.name: markup-leading-title
cases.note: Title divergence (documented v1 limit): markup right after the marker leaves the published title empty (fallback), while the editor titles the raw line.

cases.name: math-in-title
cases.note: Title divergence (documented v1 limit): inline math splits the published title like any inline construct.

cases.name: code-span-in-title
cases.note: Title divergence (documented v1 limit): an inline code span splits the published title like any inline construct.

cases.name: wikilink-in-title
cases.note: Parity holds: wikilink syntax is still plain text when the callout transform runs, so both sides title the same string.

cases.name: entity-lt-in-title
cases.note: Parity holds: a lone `<` stays text on both sides (the published HTML escapes it, so classifiers must decode entities).
